blocks.note: R is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for runs
ace as an adjective means first-rate

explanation.surface: A contest praised as excellent, with its 'runs' suggesting athletes on a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed, so it is a kind of competition.

clue.text: Good for son inside to turn down asylum

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means X takes the place of Y, a swap of one letter for another
inside says the swap happens within the word, not at its edge

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
S is the abbreviation for son
to refuse is to turn down an offer

explanation.surface: A good son is turned away when he applies for asylum.
explanation.walkthrough: In REFUSE the S becomes G.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety or shelter, the same as an asylum.

blocks.note: surface reading: Sir Edwin Landseer, the Victorian animal painter
setter's reading: a perch for a lookout, a 'land seer' watching from the mast for land

explanation.walkthrough: Split the painter's name into 'land' and 'seer': a sailor whose job is to sight land, perched at the top of the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: A theologian is given a couple of degrees in African capital

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is a Doctor of Divinity
taken as written
taken as written
two Bachelor of Arts degrees, BA and BA

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar collects two more qualifications while living in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia.

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or enclose, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a deed is an act
Il Duce was Mussolini's title; its closing E is the one DEED already has, so only three new letters go in

explanation.surface: A political move gathers support around the Italian head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter lets DUCE share its final E with DEED, a loose overlap: strictly the clue gives one E too many.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in the sense of understand is to infer, which is what deduced means.

clue.text: In a perfect world, I'd join forces to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safe within, so one part is held inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
E is the symbol for energy
to ally is to join forces

explanation.surface: An idealist would team up with others to save power.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'd is ignored, as punctuation always is in wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best possible circumstances, as things would be in a perfect world.

blocks.note: first meaning: lodging or somewhere to live
second meaning: a settlement or compromise reached between parties

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a tenancy contract; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both rooms to live in and an arrangement reached by compromise.

blocks.note: taken as written
a coaster is a small mat for a glass
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drinks mat and a single item displayed by a craftsman of fine fiddles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated Italian makers of violins.

indicators.note: read as re-sort: the letters are sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrapped present secured at a holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a seaside town but splits as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in the sense of a natural talent is an aptitude for something.

blocks.note: the foot is the bottom of something, such as a page or a hill
a pad is informal for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A historical thief hiding out in a basement apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highwayman who worked on foot, a robber of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Albert, for example, arranged prison concert

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a fresh order, as music is arranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Albert organised a gig in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, husband of Queen Victoria, held the title of Prince Consort, the spouse of a reigning queen.

indicators.note: 'some in' says only a portion of the following words is wanted, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An invitation to be charmed by the Caribbean islands under French rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or bewitch, the same as to captivate someone.

clue.text: Locum's posting is spurious reveals journalist

indicators.note: something spurious is false and not genuine, so the letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: every letter of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer exposes that a stand-in doctor's job placement is bogus.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip columnist is a journalist writing about the private lives of celebrities.

blocks.note: surface reading: someone departing from this place
setter's reading: a container where tea leaves are kept

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb of departure but is the plural noun: the dried leaves of the tea plant, stored in a small box.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin or box in which loose tea is stored.

clue.text: There's nothing, nothing like an egg

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a void is an emptiness, nothing at all

explanation.surface: A claim that nothing in the world resembles an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, from the Latin ovum for egg.

blocks.note: overt means open and plain to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some hints are plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle suggestions or connotations, things implied rather than stated.

clue.text: Female Commander-in-Chief dropped into Asian sea? Absurd

indicators.note: something dropped into a sea ends up inside it, enclosed by the water

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the Aral Sea lies in Central Asia
CIC is the abbreviation for commander-in-chief

explanation.surface: A woman military chief tossed into the sea: a ridiculous image.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical means ridiculous, like a farce, the stage comedy of silly situations.

clue.text: The Parisian's left object in lorry

indicators.note: 'has left' means gone away, so those letters depart from the word they were in

blocks.note: le is French for 'the'
an article is a thing or object

explanation.surface: A Frenchman has left something behind in a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': LE leaves ARTICLE, leaving ARTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab and trailer.

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one part encircles the other

blocks.note: the leaves of a book are its pages
taken as written
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Pages of a logbook recording the voyages of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes after the first letter of the outer word, not in the middle. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a voyage by sea, so passages are journeys.

clue.text: Crazy to stay over in German city

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: mad means crazy
to stop somewhere is to stay there

explanation.surface: It would be mad to spend a night over in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD and STOP joined, then the whole read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a city in Germany near Berlin, site of the 1945 Allied conference.

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Carved table legs on a much-loved piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' sounds like a piece of furniture, but it is the definition: a small bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small fragment or scrap, a piece of something larger.

indicators.note: doing something nervously means jittering about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hungry Greek eyeing something with anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy means having an excessive appetite, which is what voracious means.

clue.text: Console and look after one member of the government

blocks.note: a console is a cabinet housing a radio, television or controls
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Advice to comfort and care for a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a verb meaning comfort, but it is the noun for a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet minister is a senior politician sitting in the cabinet, a member of the government.

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to ring is British for to phone

explanation.surface: An instruction to call a bishop by telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to fetch it, which is one sense of get.

clue.text: CD containing lively minor hymn tune

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so the letters move into a new order
containing means holding something within, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A compact disc holds a bright little hymn in a minor key.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimond is a well-known Scottish psalm tune, usually sung to 'The Lord's my shepherd'.

clue.text: Last character to leave town in Cornwall in sackcloth and ashes?

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so that letter departs from the place-name

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the far south-west county of England

explanation.surface: The last person to quit a Cornish town is in mourning dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last character' sounds like a person but means the final letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing sackcloth and ashes was a biblical sign of repentance, an example of penance; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Run away with one chum to find fair

blocks.note: to leg it is slang for running away
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Fleeing with a friend to reach a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a fete to run off to, but it is the adjective meaning just.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful and justifiable, so it is a synonym of fair in the sense of proper.

blocks.note: taken as written
to spy something is to spot it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like the opening line of the game itself.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a children's guessing game in which players name things they can see.
